thread:
maria_g: Hey @support — customer 'AcmeAds' opened a ticket: batch rerank API returned scores that look shifted between queries. They say per-query candidate lists were correct but scores seem to belong to neighboring queries. Attached a small payload and response snippet.

dan_s: Can you paste the original request (headers + body) and the exact response? Also need their request_id and model/version.

maria_g: Request id: req_0a9c. Model: rwd-rerank-v1. Body (trimmed):
```json
{"queries":[{"q":"best laptop","candidates":["a","b","c"]},{"q":"budget laptop","candidates":["x","y"]}]}
```
Response (trimmed):
```json
{"results":[{"scores":[0.2,0.1,0.3]},{"scores":[0.8,0.7]}]}
```
Customer claims returned scores map incorrectly: for second query scores look like they belong to first, and vice versa.

support-bot: Incident created: INC-9876. Assigned to eng oncall.

oliver_k: Quick sanity checks: are they sending any compression/gzip or streaming chunking? Also what content-type header?

maria_g: They used application/json, no gzip. Large payloads sometimes use chunked encoding but not here.

elaine_p: I suspect a flattening/order bug in the batch->flat candidate mapping. If server flattens candidates then uses an offsets array, mismatch between the two (counts vs offsets) can shift boundaries.

dan_s: Trying to repro locally with the exact body. Running curl:
```bash
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/rerank/batch \n  -H "Authorization: Bearer <redacted>" \n  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \n  -d '{"queries":[{"q":"best laptop","candidates":["a","b","c"]},{"q":"budget laptop","candidates":["x","y"]}]}'
```

dan_s: Got a short log from our side for req_0a9c: 
```
INFO req_0a9c flattening candidates -> flat_count=5 offsets=[0,3] counts=[3,2]
WARN req_0a9c inference returned 5 scores, mapping back using offsets [0,2] <-- <-- aha
```

oliver_k: That log looks like bug: offsets computed twice from different code paths, and one code path used a stale variable (old offsets=[0,2]). Could be a race or reuse of a buffer between requests.

elaine_p: Edge case: if any candidate list is empty or ephemeral, code that dedups empty lists might mutate counts in place. Did the customer ever send an empty candidate array for some queries?

maria_g: Not in their sample. But they do send some queries with candidates coming from an upstream service; intermittent empties possible.

oliver_k: Repro steps I used to force the bug: run 1000 small batches concurrently where some queries include [] as candidates and others have items. I saw offsets flip when the flatten buffer pool was reused without clearing. Minimal repro attached:
```py
# repro snippet
batches = []
for i in range(1000):
  batches.append({"queries":[{"q":"q1","candidates":[]},{"q":"q2","candidates":["x"]}]})
# post batches concurrently -> ~0.6% of responses show misaligned scores
```

dan_s: TL;DR root cause: buffer/array for offsets wasn't zeroed when reused; code path A writes counts but code path B reads cached offsets from previous request. Patch: always allocate fresh offsets or explicitly set offsets[:num_queries]=0 before fill.

maria_g: Customer update: they have ~4k requests/day; only ~0.4% impacted but it's causing incorrect rankings in prod. They're requesting a hotfix/canary ASAP.

oliver_k: I'll cut a small hotfix that zeroes arrays and adds an assert in debug builds. Will push canary to 10% and monitor. PR: https://github.com/redwood/re-ranker/pull/452 (will link after CI).

elaine_p: Also adding server-side validation: if sum(counts) != flat_count then log and return 400 instead of silently mis-mapping. That will break some clients but safer. Suggest deploying validation as opt-in header X-strict-mapping:true for a week, then flip.

support-bot: Canary deployment scheduled: canary-10% at 2024-04-09T19:30:00Z. Incident INC-9876 updated.

dan_s: For customer mitigation: ask them to include per_query_counts in metadata (we support header X-perquery-counts: "3,2") — server will honor that if present and use it instead of inferring. Quick workaround until we roll the fix.

maria_g: Sent workaround and ETA to customer. They appreciated the quick follow-up.

oliver_k: Deployed canary, monitoring trace: no mapping errors in canary logs for 4h. Rolling to 50% later today. Adding unit tests for empty candidate arrays and buffer reuse.

elaine_p: Postmortem notes: root cause = reused offsets buffer not reinitialized on borrow from pool. Mitigations = zero-on-borrow, strict validation header, add CI regression.

maria_g: Thanks team :thumbsup: I'll update the ticket and close once 100% rollout confirmed.
